data.title: Every diagram is measured by mermaid's own parsers
data.description: Structure comes from the Langium grammars and mermaid core, never from regexes over the text

data.title: One rule per finding code, one file per rule
data.description: Each distinct failure is its own rule id, so it can be switched off alone

data.title: A finding fails the run, or the rule is off
data.description: There is no warning level, and an advisory pair is not a finding

data.title: No complexity rule has a fixer
data.description: Splitting a diagram changes what it says, so a human does it

data.title: A fixer refuses whenever the answer is a design choice
data.description: Contrast is repaired only with black or white, and only when it provably clears 4.5 to 1

data.title: Every edit is proven by re-parsing the document
data.description: An edit is kept only when the markdown tree and every diagram's structure are unchanged

data.title: Plugins follow the prose-gates contract
data.description: A plugin is { meta, rules } with a namespace, an apiVersion and declared categories

data.title: The Node bundle keeps mermaid and its parsers external
data.description: dist inlines this package's code and leaves its dependencies to be installed

data.title: A diagram is a code node of the markdown tree
data.description: Fences come from mdast, and offsets are mapped back to the source by line

data.title: Thresholds are rule options and flags, never environment variables
data.description: A preset and numeric overrides come from the config or a flag

data.title: A contrast profile decides who owns the label text
data.description: github scores the declared pairs, and mkdocs-material scores the host's forced text in both themes

data.title: A fixture declares what it must report in its own file
data.description: Each fixture names its expected rule ids in an expect comment, and a .fixed sibling pins its fix output

data.title: The docs site is generated from the sources the tests run
data.description: Reference pages come from RULES.md, the fixtures and examples, and the build re-checks every example

data.title: An LLM fix is committed beside its fixture and verified clean
data.description: Judgment fixes for what --fix leaves are authored once as .llm siblings, never generated at build time

data.title: Four tenets define what the tool guarantees
data.description: Readable in light and dark, renders, simple enough to follow, and extensible, and nothing else belongs in the core

data.title: A back-edge may be appended to an accepted record
data.description: The one edit an accepted record allows is adding the inverse of a relation a newer record declares

data.title: Sequence colours come from Mermaid's own theme engine
data.description: A sequence diagram is scored by theme variables Mermaid resolves on a pinned version

data.title: A host sets the page canvas, under the github profile only
data.description: Page-backed colours are scored on a canvas the caller may set, and a canvas under mkdocs-material is refused

data.title: A Material file sets a config canvas aside
data.description: A config canvas is set aside, with a note, for a file the auto profile reads as mkdocs-material

data.title: Category flags have the last word for a run
data.description: --category and --disable-category switch whole categories on or off for one run, over the config

data.title: The score counts what a reader must read, not every record the parser keeps
data.description: Control lines, markers and notes are left out, and boxes, blocks and attribute rows are counted

data.title: Every feature starts from the official parsers' output, and no parsing logic is reinvented
data.description: Diagrams are read through mermaid's parsers and markdown through mdast, never a custom parser

data.title: Markdown is read only through mdast, and reimplementing a dependency is non-compliance
data.description: No custom markdown parser, and code that duplicates an installed dependency is refactored onto it

data.title: Colour parsing and WCAG contrast come only from colorjs.io
data.description: No hand-written colour parser, luminance formula or contrast ratio

data.title: A fold is offered only as the overview half of a split
data.description: A split plan is checked by a contract and applied by a human

data.title: A split plan follows the author's structure, and refuses what it cannot draw faithfully
data.description: Regions fold first, marker states stay in their composite, and concurrency is refused

data.title: Gaps in the official parsers are recorded, each with the one narrow workaround allowed
data.description: Where mermaid exposes no source map, export or detector, the gap and its pinned workaround are listed here

data.title: Decision regions and erDiagram aggregates fold whole, named after their decision or root
data.description: A decision folds with its single-entry single-exit region, and an entity with the aggregate its root owns

data.title: Runs of alike nodes are named by range, dense meshes fold by cliques, and shared terminals stay in view
data.description: Three choices that make a split plan's groups mean something a reader can check

data.title: A group is named where a reader enters it, a dense mesh is refused, and a state that ends the flow stays in view
data.description: How a split plan names, refuses and keeps nodes so its overview reads as the diagram does

data.title: A plan lands near its target, keeps groups even and to one family, and names each stub once
data.description: How a split plan balances its groups, keeps them to one family and tells stubs apart

data.title: A pipeline stage folds across its lanes, a status stem names a family, and a stub draws each edge once
data.description: How a split plan groups a stage no edge joins, reads a family from id-led statuses, and draws edges from a whole group
